paragraphs: R. Yitzchak bar Bisna. Hyman identifies him as a native of the Land of Israel (בר א״י), a student of R. Ami and R. Assi, and a colleague of R. Abba, R. Zeira and R. Bibi, as in Zevachim 20a [supplied: זבחים כ.]: 'When Ravin came, R. Yirmeya said that R. Assi said that R. Yochanan said' — R. Yitzchak bar Bisna said before him (before R. Ami, and Ravin said the whole of it — Rashi; and Hyman argues that without basis they erased the word 'Ami' in Rashi and wrote 'R. Yirmeya'): 'Rabbi, you say so? Thus said R. Assi in the name of R. Yochanan.'

Likewise Gittin 54b [supplied: גיטין נד:]: he raised a difficulty to R. Ami and R. Assi: 'the High Priest (כה״ג) on the Day of Atonement (ביו״הכפ) will prove it.' And in Avodah Zarah 33b [supplied: ע״ז לג:]: that ר״י bar Bisna [the subject, R. Yitzchak bar Bisna] had vessels of pakisna (פקיסנא); he filled them with water, set them in the sun, and they cracked; R. Abba told him that he had lost them for nothing. And in Shekalim ch. 3 halakha 2 and ch. 8 halakha 1 [supplied: שקלים פ״ג ה״ב ופ״ח ה״א]: R. Bibi was sitting and teaching — R. Yitzchak bar Bisna spoke to him — he kicked him; R. Zerika said to him: because he asked you, you kicked him?

He [R. Bibi] said to him: because I was not myself. And in Menachot 103b [supplied: מנחות קג:] he objected to R. Bibi, and he fell silent; R. Zerika said to him: why does the master not respond, etc. And in Zevachim 43b [supplied: זבחים מג:] he objects to the words of R. Zeira [supplied ר״ז]. And in Niddah 56a [supplied: נדה נו.] we find: R. Zeira said: there is no difficulty — this refers to all of them, that to some of them; as it was taught: R. Yitzchak bar Bisna said in the name of רש״בי (abbreviation retained in Hebrew): 'in them' — one might think all of them,

etc. And indeed the baraita is cited in ת״כ פ״יא־קיד (work abbreviation and locator retained as supplied) and in Chagigah 11a [supplied: חגיגה יא.] and in Nazir 12a [supplied: נזיר יב.] anonymously; and Hyman argues that in Niddah a scribal error has crept in, and one must read that ר״ז said that ר״י bar Bisna brings a baraita in the name of רש״בי, and therefore one must read: 'that ר״י bar Bisna said: as רש״בי teaches, saying' — and Hyman considers this clear. He is likewise mentioned in Yoma 5a [supplied: יומא ה.], and in Yevamot 113b [supplied: יבמות קיג:], that the keys of the ב״המד (Hebrew retained; apparently the study house) were lost to him; he came before
R. Pedat (son of ר״א, in Hyman’s parenthesis), and he instructed him to bring a child, etc.

notes.text: Hyman's 'בר א״י' is expanded here as 'Palestinian-born' per standard abbreviation, but this expansion is not in the frozen acronym registry; flagged as uncertain.

Unknown acronyms kept in Hebrew: ב״המד, ביו״הכפ, ר״ז, ר״א, רש״בי. Translation of 'ר״ז' as R. Zerika/Zeira and 'ר״א' as R. Elazar is tentative; 'רש״בי' rendered R. Shimon bar Yochai conventionally but not registry-verified.
Hebrew pakisna and the Aramaic text of Avodah Zarah and Shekalim are partially paraphrased; the word בעט (kicked) and 'פקיסנא' retained as in source with uncertain sense.
Hyman's remark that Rashi's text was wrongly altered and that Niddah contains a scribal error are Hyman's assertions, preserved as such, not independently verified.

In the consulted Zevachim 20a text the first chain has Rabbi Ami, whereas Hyman supplies Assi; the consulted Rashi comment explicitly says “before R’ Ami.” This supports a current digital reading, not Hyman’s account of an erased or replaced printed word. The consulted Niddah 56a paragraphs name Yitzchak be-Rabbi Bisna with Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, while Hyman supplies bar Bisna and argues for a different transmission formula; his emphatic correction remains attributed. The consulted Chagigah 11a paragraphs give the baraita anonymously. The intended parallel in supplied Nazir 12a and the literal ת״כ פ״יא־קיד locator remain unverified in this review. Yevamot 113b continues onto 114a with Pedat’s instruction involving children; the passage does not resolve Hyman’s parenthetical father ר״א. The supplied pakisna vessel term is retained, and none of these comparisons admits a genealogy, teacher relationship, identity merge, or Hebrew correction. The consulted Shekalim parallels use Rav Beiva/Beivai; 8:1 has Zerikan where 3:2 has Zerika. These forms remain source-specific comparisons. Catalogue-routed Sifra, Shemini, Chapter 11 was read in full in its nine returned paragraphs, but did not establish the intended baraita or the literal supplied locator; this is not a claim about all Sifra editions. The attempted Nazir search removed its book filter and returned other works, so it supplies no evidence for the intended passage or its absence.

Zevachim 20a gives Rabbi Ami in the first transmission chain and Rabbi Assi in Bisna’s response. The consulted Rashi also says the response was before Rabbi Ami and that Ravin reported the whole exchange. Niddah 56a has Yitzchak be-Rabbi Bisna in both introductions, linked to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai with two different formulas. Hyman’s account of the Rashi change and his proposed Niddah reading remain attributed to him.

The anonymous parallel about the lentil-sized portion occurs in Chagigah 11a and in the consulted Nazir 52a, where Rav Yehudah of Diskarta introduces it. Hyman prints Nazir 12a. The consulted Venice 1545 Sifra, Shemini, chapter 7, paragraph 6, gives the same exposition and Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda’s alternative benchmark. The numbering of Hyman’s precise Sifra edition remains unverified. In Yevamot 113b–114a, Pedat suggests taking a boy and a girl to walk there so that if they find the lost study-house keys, they bring them. The passage gives no patronymic for Pedat. Hyman’s parenthetical ר״א stays unexpanded.

In the printed Dikdukei Soferim on Beitzah 22a, p. 51, the manuscript column has Yitzchak bar Bisna where the printed column and the consulted Davidson text have Hinnana bar Bisna. This is a local name variant.
